paper.title: Adapting to Misspecification in Contextual Bandits with Offline Regression Oracles

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-armed stochastic contextual bandit with misspecified model class F and offline regression oracle
unmapped: access to an offline regression oracle on F with a known, valid estimation rate xi(n, zeta) (Assumption 1); the learner knows xi
misspecification measured by unknown average squared misspecification B (max over kernels in K(F) of min_f mean squared error); B not known to learner
settings.definition_quote: At every time-step $t \in [T]$, the environment draws a context $x_t\in\Xscript$ and reward vector $\smash{r_t \in [0,1]^K}$ from a fixed but unknown distribution $D$. ... We denote by $\sqrt{B}$ the \emph{average misspecification} error relative to $\F$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit with misspecified model class F (lower bound)
unmapped: misspecification measured by average squared misspecification B relative to F
settings.definition_quote: We prove a new lower bound on the regret overhead due to misspecification for the stochastic contextual bandit setting in terms of the average misspecification error $\sqrt{B}$

algorithms.name: Safe-FALCON
requires_knowledge_of: estimation rate xi of the regression oracle

symbols.B: average squared misspecification of F (constant in Assumption 1; sqrt(B) is the average misspecification error)
symbols.Xi_sum: sum_{t=tau_1+1}^T sqrt(xi(tau_{m(t)-1}-tau_{m(t)-2}, delta/m(t)^2)), xi the oracle estimation rate, m(t) the epoch of round t

conditions: regression oracle satisfies Assumption 1 with known valid estimation rate xi
tuning: initial epoch length tau_1 >= 2, doubling epochs

source.label: thm:main-theorem
source.quote: Suppose the regression algorithm used in $\SafeFalcon$ satisfies \Cref{ass:main-assumption}. Then with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $\SafeFalcon$ attains the following regret guarantee: R_T \leq \ordO( \sqrt{KB}\;T + \sqrt{K}\sum_{t=\tau_1+1}^{T} \sqrt{\xi(\tau_{m(t)-1}-\tau_{m(t)-2}, \frac{\delta}{(m(t))^2})} ).

results.notes: R_T is realized regret vs. the Bayes-optimal policy pi*(x)=argmax_a f*(x,a); holds w.p. 1-delta. B unknown to the algorithm. Number printed assumed Theorem 1 (restatable, first theorem).

symbols.rho: exponent of the estimation rate, in (0,1]
symbols.rho_p: log exponent rho' of the estimation rate, >= 0
symbols.comp_F: complexity measure comp(F) of the model class

conditions: regression oracle satisfies Assumption 1 with estimation rate xi(n,zeta)=C ln^{rho'}(n) ln(1/zeta) comp(F)/n^rho for n>=n_0 (1 otherwise)

source.label: cor:common-rate
source.quote: Suppose the regression algorithm used in $\SafeFalcon$ satisfies \Cref{ass:main-assumption} with estimation rate of the form given by \eqref{eq:common-rate}. Then with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $\SafeFalcon$ attains the following regret guarantee: R_T \leq \ordO( \sqrt{KB}\;T + \sqrt{KT^{2-\rho}\ln^{\rho'}(T)\ln(\frac{\ln(T)}{\delta})\comp(\F)} ).

results.notes: Specialisation of Theorem 1 to polynomial estimation rates.

conditions: applies to any probability kernel p in the convex hull of the kernel set K(F) (i.e., algorithms that play randomized policies induced by kernels in conv K(F))
constructed model class F (context-independent models) and instance with noiseless rewards, uniform contexts

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consider any $K\geq 2$ and $B\in [0,1/(2K)]$. One can construct a model class $\F$ and a stochastic contextual bandit instance with $K$ arms. Such that the average misspecification error is $\sqrt{B}$. And for any probability kernel $p$ in the convex hull of the kernel set $\kernelSet$, the expected instantaneous regret of the induced randomized policy can be lower bounded by: ... \geq \Omega(\sqrt{KB})

results.notes: Bound on expected per-round (instantaneous) regret of any kernel in conv K(F); paper informally implies Omega(sqrt(KB) T) cumulative regret for algorithms using such kernels a constant fraction of time. Proof gives exact value sqrt((K-1)B) >= sqrt(KB/2).
